content:
After a two-year hiatus without updates, Apple is developing a new generation of iMac with the M6 chip and will refresh its colour options, with a launch anticipated "before the end of the year," according to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman.

The iMac is not updated frequently — it previously skipped the M2 and M5 chip generations, and to this day has not offered a larger screen size option, with Apple instead steering high-end users towards the Mac Studio or Mac mini paired with a Studio Display. Despite this, Apple is still preparing to release a new version with the M6 chip.

Gurman noted that this update will bring "some new colour options," though he did not mention specifics. Apple made slight adjustments to its colours in the 2024 M4 version, but in reality the seven colour options remained unchanged, with only minor tonal differences. The new iMac is also expected to launch before the end of this year:

This means the autumn will be quite significant for Mac. There will be a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen and Tandem OLED, a new entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip, a new Mac Studio with the M5 Max and M5 Ultra (depending on supply availability), and a new iMac with the M6 chip. Another possibility is a new Mac mini with the M6 and M5 Pro, though that product is expected to launch at a later date.

Apple's M6 chip will be the first Mac chip manufactured using the new 2nm process, but reportedly there will not be M6 Pro, M6 Max, or M6 Ultra versions — instead, Apple will accelerate the release of the M7 series chips.
